title: Credit Controller
description:
MacKenzie King are working with a successful, growing business based in Woolpit to find an organised and proactive Credit Controller to join their supportive Accounts team. Previous experience working in a high-volume credit control department is essential as this position will be working as part of a small team handling credit control for locations across the UK, so being organised and used to managing a high-volume workload will also be essential. You will be responsible for chasing outstanding payments, running credit checks and screening for fraud risks, as well as collaborating with the depot manager.

Key tasks and responsibilities
- Overseeing high-density day-to-day accounts receivable, tracking payments, and actively managing cash collections across multiple businesses.
- Credit Checking & Risk Management: Conducting rigorous credit evaluations on new and existing contractors, setting appropriate credit limits, monitoring transactions for red flags, and identifying potential invoice fraud or unusual payment behaviours.
- Partnering with Sales & Operations: Working hand-in-hand with our sales teams and depot managers to onboard new clients smoothly, balance risk with revenue goals, and resolve billing disputes quickly to keep cash moving while nurturing strong customer relationships.
- Streamlining Cash Flow: Minimising Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and running regular aging and risk reports for senior leadership.

Qualifications and experience
- Proven experience managing high-volume credit control or accounts receivable, ideally within the construction or a related project-based industry.
- Strong expertise in credit checking, financial risk mitigation, and fraud detection.
- Excellent interpersonal skills with a proven track record of partnering successfully with sales teams and depot managers to drive both collection and commercial success.
- Comfortable juggling high-volume ledgers and competing priorities across multiple business entities with solid Excel skills and a sharp eye for detail.

To find out more about this opportunity, please contact Ben at MacKenzie King.

title: Support Administrator
description:
Accounts Support Administrator

A Fantastic Opportunity to Start Your Career in Accountancy

Are you highly organised, detail-oriented, and looking to build a long-term career in Finance and Accountancy?

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is keen to develop a career within an Accounts environment. Whether you already have some office administration experience or are looking to take your first step into Finance, full training and support will be provided to help you develop your skills and knowledge.

Working alongside an experienced and supportive Accounts team, you will gain hands-on exposure to a wide range of accounting functions and processes, with clear opportunities for progression as your confidence and expertise grow. - Has previous administration or office-based experience
- Is highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Enjoys working with data and systems
- Has good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Possesses strong communication skills and a professional telephone manner
- Is eager to learn and develop new skills
- Has an interest in pursuing a career within Accounts, Finance or Accountancy
- Works well both independently and as part of a team

Previous experience within an Accounts or Finance environment would be beneficial but is not essential, as training will be provided.

Training & Development

We are committed to supporting your professional development and will provide full training on our systems, processes, and procedures.

As your knowledge and confidence develop, you will have the opportunity to gain practical experience in:

title: Aquarius Relationship and Placement Coordinator

- Strong knowledge of Commercial Combined insurance, with a focus on the SME sector

- Proven ability to manage and coordinate insurance placements or facility business

- Effective communication skills, both written and verbal

- Proactive and solutions-focused
- Strong relationship builder with a cooperative approach
- Comfortable working in a busy, evolving, and digitally enabled environment

Aquarius is a strategic initiative designed to digitise and enhance SME placements, delivering efficient, data-led placement solutions for brokers, clients, and insurer partners. The role provides a unique opportunity to be at the centre of a growing, high-profile facility and contribute to its continued success and expansion.

title: Health Safety Coordinator
description:
Health & Safety Coordinator

Temporary Position
Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm

The Role

We are recruiting for a proactive and organised Health & Safety Coordinator to support the day-to-day facilities and compliance activities of our client's business. This is a varied role responsible for coordinating maintenance, managing contractors, maintaining compliance records, and supporting health and safety initiatives across the site.

Key Responsibilities

Facilities Coordination
- Coordinate planned and reactive maintenance activities.
- Manage relationships with contractors and service providers, including cleaning, security, and maintenance suppliers.
- Arrange repairs, servicing, inspections, and compliance visits.
- Monitor and resolve facilities-related issues in a timely manner.
- Support the upkeep of a safe, compliant, and efficient working environment.

Health & Safety
- Support the implementation of company health and safety procedures.
- Assist with workplace inspections, risk assessments, and safety audits.
- Coordinate fire safety checks, emergency procedures, and evacuation planning.
- Maintain records of accidents, incidents, near misses, and corrective actions.
- Support incident investigations and ensure reporting procedures are followed.
- Identify and escalate potential risks and hazards.

Compliance & Administration
- Maintain accurate health and safety records and compliance documentation.
- Coordinate statutory compliance activities, including PAT testing, fire alarm testing, emergency lighting checks, legionella monitoring, and contractor documentation.
- Ensure all certifications and records are up to date and audit-ready.
- Produce reports and management information relating to facilities and health & safety.
- Utilise facilities management systems, health & safety software, and Excel to track actions and maintain records.

Skills & Experience

Essential
- Previous experience in a Facilities Coordinator, Facilities Management, Workplace Coordinator, or similar role.
- Knowledge of UK Health & Safety legislation, including Health & Safety at Work Act, RIDDOR, and COSHH.
- Experience supporting risk assessments, workplace inspections, and audits.
- Experience managing contractors and coordinating maintenance activities.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.

title: Town Planner - Tentatively Good CVS
description:
Town Planner

Location: Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk
Salary: £30,000/£35,000
Working Pattern: Hybrid / flexible working
Employment Type: Full-time, permanent

The Benefits
- Competitive salary based on experience
- Hybrid and flexible working to support a healthy work-life balance
- Generous annual leave
- Above-industry-average employer pension contribution
- Private healthcare / healthcare benefits
- Annual salary reviews
- Free parking
- Maternity and paternity benefits
- Strong opportunities for career progression and professional development
- Support for professional qualifications and CPD
- The opportunity to work across a diverse portfolio of rural, residential, commercial and strategic land projects
- A collaborative, client-focused working environment within an established multidisciplinary consultancy

About the Role

An established and growing planning consultancy is looking to appoint a Planner to join its team in Bury St Edmunds.

This is an excellent opportunity for a planning professional looking to develop their career within a consultancy that works across agricultural, rural, residential and commercial sectors.

The successful candidate will work on a varied portfolio of projects, providing planning advice from the early feasibility and appraisal stages through to planning applications, appeals and project delivery.

The business has a strong focus on providing practical, commercially minded planning advice and helping clients identify development opportunities and navigate the planning process effectively.

Key Responsibilities

As a Planner, your responsibilities will include:
- Undertaking planning research, site appraisals and feasibility studies
- Preparing planning appraisals, planning statements and supporting documentation
- Preparing and submitting planning applications, including outline, full and change-of-use applications
- Preparing and submitting planning appeals
- Providing pre-application planning advice
- Supporting the promotion of strategic development sites and land
- Preparing representations in relation to Local Plans and planning policy
- Advising clients on planning strategy and development potential
- Liaising with local planning authorities, consultants and other stakeholders
- Attending client meetings and site visits
- Assisting with negotiations with planning officers
- Attending planning committees, hearings and public inquiries where required
- Providing advice relating to Section 106 agreements, Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and other planning obligations
- Supporting multidisciplinary project teams and coordinating external consultants
- Assisting with rural planning matters, including agricultural and rural diversification projects
- Keeping up to date with changes to planning legislation, policy and guidance

The role offers exposure to a broad range of projects, including residential development, commercial schemes, rural diversification, strategic land promotion and agricultural planning.

Requirements

The ideal candidate will have:
- A degree or postgraduate qualification in Town Planning, ideally RTPI accredited
- Previous experience within a planning consultancy, local authority or related planning environment
- A good understanding of UK planning legislation, policy and procedures
- Experience preparing planning applications, appraisals and/or planning statements
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Excellent report-writing and organisational skills
- The ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
- Confidence dealing with clients, planning officers and other consultants
- A proactive approach and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team
- Membership of, or progress towards, MRTPI would be advantageous
- A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle is desirable due to the nature of the role and site visits

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to join a well-established consultancy with a strong presence in the agricultural, environmental and planning sectors. The planning team works across East Anglia and nationally, with projects ranging from individual planning applications through to larger-scale development and strategic land opportunities.

There is scope for the successful candidate to develop their technical expertise, client base and career, with professional development and progression encouraged.

Interested?

If you are interested in this opportunity and would like to find out more, please email your CV to .

title: Receptionist / Admin Assistant

title: Administrative Assistant
description: Woolpit Health Centre has an exciting opportunity for an Administrative Assistant to join our friendly and supportive Administration Team. We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, reliable and organised, with a willingness to learn and develop their skills. This role would suit someone who is new to administration and looking to start a career in healthcare, as well as someone with previous administrative or healthcare experience who is looking for their next opportunity. Previous experience within a GP practice or healthcare setting would be beneficial but is not essential, as full training and support will be provided to the right candidate. The successful applicant will assist with a range of administrative tasks to support the smooth day-to-day running of the Health Centre. We are looking for someone who is: Friendly, approachable and professional Well organised and able to manage a variety of tasks Reliable and willing to learn new skills Able to work accurately with good attention to detail Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team Flexible and adaptable in responding to the needs of the Practice Committed to providing a high standard of service to patients and colleagues The role will involve providing general administrative support to the Practice and its staff, as directed by the Administration Lead. Manage patient, healthcare professional and third-party enquiries via email, telephone and face-to-face. Process clinical records, correspondence, pathology results and workflow tasks accurately and efficiently. Scan, uploaded, code and allocate clinical documentation for GP review and maintain accurate patient records. Manage patient registrations and medical records through Healthtech-1. Support reception and clinical teams with Anima online requests and administrative workflows. Support QOF targets by contacting patients regarding annual health reviews and appointments. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with NHS policies, procedures and data protection requirements. Undertake general administrative duties and provide additional support to the management and GP team as required. General Administrative Duties Monitor the practice generic email inbox, responding to enquiries from patients, healthcare professionals, and third parties in a timely and professional manner. Process and transfer clinical records accurately, allocating documents to appropriate clinical workflows for GP review. Scan, upload and code clinical correspondence onto the patient clinical system while maintaining accurate healthcare records. Distribute daily pathology and laboratory results to clinicians for review through the clinical system. Monitor and action tasks within clinical and workflow systems efficiently to support smooth practice operations. Process and manage administrative and clinical correspondence through the Anima workflow system. Handle patient, staff, and healthcare professional enquiries effectively, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Answer incoming calls, transferred calls appropriately, and resolved queries in a professional and confidential manner. Register and process new patient registrations through the Healthtech-1 portal, including medical records and deductions. Carry out general administrative duties including scanning, photocopying, filing, and document management. Support the delivery of QOF (Quality Outcomes Framework) targets by contacting patients regarding annual health reviews and appointments. To support the reception team with processing online requests via Anima alongside the duty GPs Maintain confidentiality and adhere to practice protocols to ensure consistent, high-quality patient care and compliance with NHS procedures. Undertake additional duties as required by the Practice Manager, Operations Manager, Administration Lead, or the GP team.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Part time member of staff to cover approx. 20 hours per week, with some weekend working. This is an exciting role that will include working within our reception. The role is very varied with every day being different. Your role is important to make sure that patients will be receiving the very best of care that they expect. Full support and training will be given. Prospective applicants are welcome to contact the Deputy Practice Manager, Abby Lake for an informal visit or further information. This position is not available to those that live overseas or require sponsorship to work in the UK. Good communication skills are essential.The role includes communicating with patients and colleagues, either face to face, via the telephone, sending texts, typing letters or emails. You will be Flexible and the ability to organise your time is important to the role. You will be working in our reception area dealing with patients within the surgery, with repeat prescription requests, the administration of medical reports or general queries. Scanning and clinically coding letters from other clinical settings, arranging to call patients for their regular chronic illness checks or managing our e-consultation system. You will be organised and work to efficient systems. You may be typing and organising the referrals to different organisations. You will be able to work within a team but also under your own initiative. To receive and book in patient's for Nurses and Doctors. To make appointments for patients. Answer telephone and deal with any resulting enquiries/requests. Accept and action all requests for repeat prescriptions whether requested in person, by e-mail, by fax or by post. To extract medical records for appointments, telephone messages, prescriptions etc. Complete the necessary documentation for temporary residents, immediate necessary treatment and emergency treatment. Charge and collect all private fees for non contracted work. Filing of various documents as required. Receive transport requests from patients and action them according to Surgery policy. Action on a daily basis any requests for home visits. Take messages for the District Nurses. Deal with incoming/outgoing post. Make tea/coffee for Doctors/Staff as required. Keep the reception area neat and tidy. Keep Doctors consulting rooms neat and tidy and clear of medical records and prescriptions that have been completed. Lock away prescriptions, make sure the surgery is as clear of filing as possible in the time allowed, ready for the morning staff. Set alarm if building is empty; lock doors and windows. Electronic summarising of patient medical records Scanning of documents into electronic patient records Typing letters either dictated by clinicians or under own discretion Dealing with emails/e-consultations by using strict protocols to signpost patient to the correct place. Adhere fully to the practice confidentiality and safeguarding policies. Undertake any other duties as may be determined from time to time commensurate with the job role.
